 KRA announces new deadline for filing individual income tax returns
 Tuesday 10th November, 2026 01:41 PM | 
 By Sharon Atieno 
 Times Tower, the head offices of Kenya Revenue Authority. PHOTO/@KRACorporate/X 
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has announced a new deadline for filing individual income tax returns, moving the annual submission date from June 30 to April 30, starting in 2027.
 The change means taxpayers filing their 2026 income tax returns will be required to submit them by April 30, 2027, two months earlier than the previous deadline.
 In a post shared on its X account on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, KRA said the new deadline would take effect on January 1, 2027, under the Finance Act 2026.
 “The new deadline is 30th April,” the authority stated in its announcement, urging taxpayers to mark their calendars and prepare for the change.
 post by KRA.PHOTO/screengrab by People Daily Digital/ @KRACare /X 
 KRA advised taxpayers to plan ahead, file their returns early and remain compliant with their tax obligations.
 The adjustment gives individual taxpayers a shorter period to prepare and submit their annual returns, making early preparation important for those who typically wait until the final weeks before the June deadline.
 New deadline takes effect in 2027
 Under the new arrangement, taxpayers will need to ensure their 2026 income details are ready before the end of April 2027.
 The previous June 30 deadline gave individuals additional time to organise their records, calculate their income and complete the filing process.
 With the new date, taxpayers may need to review their employment income statements, relevant financial records and other supporting documents earlier to avoid last-minute delays.
 KRA has encouraged taxpayers to familiarise themselves with the revised deadline and make the necessary arrangements ahead of its implementation.
 What taxpayers need to know
 The authority’s announcement signals a change to the annual filing calendar, making it important for individuals to confirm their obligations and prepare their returns within the revised period.
 Taxpayers should also ensure that the information submitted is accurate and that they retain relevant documents to support their declarations.
 The new deadline applies to the filing of 2026 individual income tax returns, which will fall due in April 2027.
 Late filing can attract penalties
 The announcement comes as KRA continues to enforce tax compliance requirements for individuals and businesses.
 In a separate reminder concerning monthly Pay As You Earn (PAYE) obligations, KRA requires employers to file returns and remit tax deducted from employees’ salaries by the ninth day of the following month.
 Employers who miss the monthly deadline face penalties and interest, highlighting the importance of meeting statutory tax obligations.
 Taxpayers are therefore encouraged to monitor KRA’s official communication channels for further guidance on the revised annual filing deadline and prepare their returns well before April 30, 2027.
